Author: Noell Barnidge
Title: ST. ANDREW'S SAINTS - SAINTS PLAYERS ARE MARCHING FOR A VICTORY
Summary: A Savannah Morning News preview of Bob Curley's second St. Andrew's football season, including preseason expectations, key returning players, and the published roster.
SourceCitation: Noell Barnidge, "ST. ANDREW'S SAINTS - SAINTS PLAYERS ARE MARCHING FOR A VICTORY," Savannah Morning News (GA), August 19, 2005, Page 11, Section: HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL 2005.
Transcript:
ST. ANDREW'S SAINTS - SAINTS PLAYERS ARE MARCHING FOR A VICTORY

Despite being winless and outscored by 362 points last season, the St. Andrew's football team, is optimistic about this season.

The Saints, 0-10 last season, scored 21 points. They gave up 383.

But they aren't giving up on the coming season.

"We will definitely improve over last season," St. Andrew's second-year head coach Bob Curley said. "Every positive is a 100 percent improvement over last year."

This season, St. Andrew's plays the same 10 teams in the exact order in which it played them last season. With a more creative Pro-Set offense, Curley anticipates the Saints will not be held scoreless until the ninth game of the season, as they were last season.

"We're real young this year, but we were even younger last year," said Curley, who has three seniors and a junior among his 22 players. "I don't have much maturity, but I have some size."

Four players are over 200 pounds. The size of linemen Jamie Cooper (6-foot-1, 230 pounds), Ben Oliver (6-3, 260), Adam Fox (6-1, 210), and Tim Svoboda (5-7, 205) should benefit St. Andrew's.

Conditioning also will determine St. Andrew's success, as Curley plans to have most of his players playing on offense and defense.

"Particularly the older fellas," he said. "I just got through telling them that they better be prepared to play about 80 plays."

St. Andrew's three seniors - Cooper, Frank Howard (5-7, 160, RB-DE) and Garrett McCarthy (5-10, 165, RB-LB) - are being counted on to provide leadership.

Curley said Frank Howard and junior Jeff Howard (5-10, 165, RB-DB) will get the bulk of the carries at running back. In the passing game, sophomore wide receiver Patrick Maleki (6-3, 180) will be the primary target.

"This year, we'll have a better corps of skill position players," Curley said. "We haven't gotten into the defensive side of the ball yet (as of Aug. 4). We only started practice on Monday, so we haven't had a chance to fine-tune anything on defense."

Three players are competing for the starting job at quarterback. Sophomore Bubby Pavlo (5-9, 125), the backup last season to team co-captain Matt Knight, who graduated, is being given "a long, hard look" by the Saints' coaching staff. Pavlo is competing for the job with two freshmen, Jon Hope (5-10, 155) and Jim Kingston (5-9, 130).

St. Andrew's smallest margin of defeat last season was a 6-0 loss to Memorial Day in a non-league game. This season, St. Andrew's will be the visitor when the teams play Aug. 26.

In South Carolina Independent School Association 3-AA competition, St. Andrew's lost to Hilton Head Christian (42-0), Hilton Head Prep (40-0), First Baptist Church of Charleston, (49-0) and Colleton Prep Academy (48-14) in four consecutive weeks.

This season, Curley said, "We expect to be competitive in our region."
